Maia vs Dust

Choose a Slack coworker or a broader AI operations platform.

Dust gives companies a multi-model platform for agents across apps. Maia centers each coworker on the Slack channel where the team asks and reviews.

The short answer

Dust is a broad company AI platform with shared agents, reusable skills, knowledge spaces, multiple models, Slack and Teams integrations, scheduled work, and enterprise governance. Maia is more opinionated about where collaboration happens. It gives each Slack channel a coworker with its own guidance, memory, connections, and approvers.

Dust has the stronger documented record for organizations that want an agent platform across apps and enterprise deployment options. Maia is a focused fit when the Slack thread should remain the visible work record and the channel should own the coworker's operating context.

A customer issue workflow

A support channel receives a complex customer issue. The team needs a sourced summary, a ticket draft, a proposed reply, and a follow-up reminder. The source set includes the Slack thread, approved product notes, and permitted customer records.

With Maia, the channel coworker follows support-specific guidance and keeps its draft in the thread. A support lead can correct the diagnosis, approve the ticket write, and review the reply before it is sent. The channel retains the correction for similar work, while another channel can keep different instructions and tools.

Dust can build the same kind of flow with a shared agent, company knowledge, Slack auto-reply, and scheduled or event-driven workflows. Dust's Spaces, Pods, and agent workspace give AI operations teams a broader place to design and govern agents beyond Slack. Both products support shared channel work, multiple models, and scheduled agents.

Choose Maia when

Choose Maia when adoption should start with the channel and its existing work habits. The team can teach a coworker in context, see its work in threads, and name approvers for connected actions. Each person connects their own app account, so Maia uses the requester's existing access for connected work.

Maia's pooled-credit offer may suit companies with many occasional users, but pricing should be compared only after running the same tasks. Maia credits and Dust credits are not equivalent units.

Choose Dust when

Choose Dust when the company needs an agent platform that extends beyond Slack. Dust publishes a broad model catalog, connector list, shared agent controls, audit and usage analytics, SCIM, US and EU residency, and enterprise single-tenant deployment. Its public material also provides more evidence of adoption and enterprise readiness.

Dust is a good fit for an AI operations group that wants a dedicated environment to create, distribute, and govern many agents. Its Slack workflows can invoke agents on schedules or events, while its main workspace supports deeper administration.

Test the decisive details

Run the same support task in both products. Record how each exposes source citations, memory, requester identity, approvals, tool calls, and audit history. Test an auto-reply or routine with incomplete data and a proposed external write. Ask whether Slack actions use shared credentials, personal connections, or a service identity.

For cost, choose three representative tasks and record actual consumption. Estimate active users and task frequency. Dust currently publishes per-seat credit plans, while Maia advertises pooled organization credits. A useful comparison explains both workload and access model.

Common questions

Is Dust Slack-native?

Dust has an official Slack app, auto-reply behavior, and Slack workflows. Its product center also includes its own workspace and other integrations. Maia makes Slack channels and DMs the primary interface.

Which product supports more models?

Both support multiple model providers. Dust publicly advertises more than 20 models. Maia offers model choice and routing, but buyers should compare the exact models available in their plans.

Which has stronger enterprise controls?

Dust has the stronger published record today, including SCIM, residency options, audit analytics, and single-tenant deployment. Maia has organization policy and administration, but buyers should verify required controls in the current product.
